newsitem.title: GREECE: Cyprus stock exchange working on paperless trading.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stock exchange working on paperless trading.

text.p: The Cyprus stock exchange (CSE), where trading is presently by open outcry, is working on share dematerialisation and expects paperless trading by February 28, 1998, its manager told reporters in Athens.
"Trading is still in open outcry form but will give way to an automated, electronic screen-based system by year-end 1997," said CSE manager Nontas Metaxas.
Metaxas, on a short visit to Athens, met with Athens stock exchange president Manolis Xanthakis and brokers' association (SMEHA) president Panagiotis Kondalexis.
"Dematerialisation has started and we expect it will be completed by February 28, 1998," Metaxas added. The transfer of securities will then be performed through an electronic book-entry system.

Presently 91 securities issued by 41 listings are traded on the exchange including fully and partly-paid shares, rights, warrants and corporate bonds. It will soon begin listing government debt paper, Metaxas said.
Member brokers of the CSE currently number 17 but will soon become 20. Trading hours are 11:00-12:30 local and the daily volatility limit is 15 percent.
And there are rumours that Athens bourse member National Securities is considering membership in the CSE.

Brokers' commissions, presently under a fixed rate regime, will also be deregulated. All shares are issued in registered form and short-selling is prohibited. Market capitalisation is about 1.5 billion Cyprus pounds.
The CSE keeps close contact with the Athens bourse and has often tapped its knowhow and advice. It will celebrate its first birthday on March 29.

"We are steering the exchange towards a course of internationalisation. Naturally, Greece is the first country where a good relationship can flourish," said Metaxas, noting that the Cyprus economy presently meets all Maastricht requirements for EMU.
The CSE council, appointed by the government, is responsible for management of the bourse and policy implementation. The capital market commission has only a veto power over CSE council decisions.
